summary: A minority-party floor speaker begins with thanks and a promise to be constructive, then says plainly and firmly where the majority is wrong and why they must vote no.
realLife: Minority leaders in Hawaii and Colorado addressed the chair and the majority with courtesy, praising staff and the chamber, and said disagreement would stay respectful. One promised never to oppose a bill without offering an alternative; another said so in a floor vote on a hard issue and called the process rushed; a third reminded the chamber how many residents his side speaks for.
sources: Beth Fukumoto Chang, Hawaii House minority leader, opening day remarks, Jan 20, 2016: https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2016/docs/HouseMinorityLeaderFukumotoOpeningRemarks.pdf

Aaron Ling Johanson and Beth Fukumoto, Hawaii House minority leader and floor leader, floor speeches on Senate Bill 1 in special session, 2013 (excerpts): https://hawaiifreepress.com/Articles-Main/ID/11067/Excerpts-from-House-GOP-Floor-Speeches
Rep. Caldwell, Colorado House minority leader, opening day speech, Jan 15, 2026: https://www.coloradohouserepublicans.com/news/minority-leader-caldwell-opening-day-speech
